projectContext.occupancy: Group R-2 stated by the question
projectContext.configuration: Scissor stair with entrance doors 15 feet apart

exactPassages: Stairs sharing any common wall, floor, ceiling, scissor stair assembly, or other enclosure shall be counted as one exit stairway.

testCase.question: Our Group R-2 building has a scissor stair with the two stair entrance doors located 15 feet apart. Can the two stairs be counted as two separate exits?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The 15-foot separation alone is not enough. Under the general rule, stairs sharing a scissor-stair assembly are counted as one exit stairway. However, the Group R-2 exception permits the stairs to share the assembly and be counted separately when the stair enclosures and the construction separating the stairs have at least a 2-hour fire-resistance rating and are constructed of masonry or a masonry equivalent in accordance with department rules. The exit doors must also be at least 15 feet apart. Confirm the occupancy group, enclosure rating, separating construction, and material before concluding that the exception applies.

answer.conclusion: Conditionally yes. Although stairs sharing a scissor stair assembly ordinarily must be counted as one exit stairway, the selected Group R-2 exception permits stairs to share a scissor stair assembly if its stated separation and construction conditions are met. The reported 15-foot separation of the stair exit doors meets the exception’s minimum door-separation threshold (“no less than 15 feet”). Thus, the two scissor-stair components may be counted as two separate exit stairways only if the required 2-hour, masonry-or-masonry-equivalent enclosure and intervening separation construction are provided in accordance with department rules. [§1007.1.1, Passage IDs 04fbbc5b-2962-496f-8e9c-960fb7c0b5a7; 0adebc93-94b2-4390-b93f-d4c4c10a0dbe]

testCase.title: Occupancy classification of a residential multipurpose room

exactPassages: A room or space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons and accessory to another occupancy shall be classified as a Group B occupancy or as part of that occupancy, except that the number of plumbing fixtures for such a room or space is permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for assembly occupancies.

For areas without fixed seating, the occupant load shall be not less than that number determined by dividing the floor area under consideration by the occupant load factor assigned to the function of the space as set forth in Table 1004.1.3.

testCase.question: A 900-net-square-foot multipurpose room in an apartment building will normally contain tables and chairs and is only for residents. Does it need to be classified as Group A-3?
testCase.expectedConclusion: For an unconcentrated assembly arrangement with tables and chairs, Table 1004.1.3 uses 15 net square feet per occupant. A 900-net-square-foot room therefore has a calculated occupant load of 60 people. Because that is fewer than 75 occupants, and assuming the room is accessory to the residential occupancy, BC 303.1.3 permits it to be classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy it serves rather than as Group A. The result depends on the actual net area, furniture arrangement, intended activities, and whether the room is truly accessory to the residential use.

answer.conclusion: Conditionally, no. If the room is used for assembly purposes and is accessory to the apartment-building occupancy, its calculated occupant load is 60 persons (900 net square feet ÷ 15 net square feet per person for “Unconcentrated (tables and chairs)”). Because 60 is fewer than 75, Section 303.1.3 directs that it be classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy to which it is accessory, rather than requiring Group A-3 classification. The plumbing-fixture count for the room may nevertheless be calculated under the assembly-occupancy requirements. [Section 132, Passage 06782ff8-5347-4a3c-b2dc-2f9c52ee7c7d; Section 2152, Passages 781451d5-5633-43f3-aa9f-9603de6acc0a, 3bef06d8-a897-40d0-b669-f4d3d16a2c01, 5d07e354-c603-48be-a6f5-fadd2c52a928]

testCase.title: Plumbing fixtures for an accessory assembly space

projectContext.potentialClassification: Group B under the accessory assembly provision

exactPassages: A room or space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons and accessory to another occupancy shall be classified as a Group B occupancy or as part of that occupancy, except that the number of plumbing fixtures for such a room or space is permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for assembly occupancies.

Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 403.1. Types of occupancies not shown in Table 403.1 shall be considered individually by the commissioner. The number of occupants shall be determined by the New York City Building Code. Occupancy classification shall be determined in accordance with the New York City Building Code.

The number of fixtures for building or nonaccessory tenant space used for assembly purposes by fewer than 75 persons and classified as Group B occupancy in accordance with Section 303.1, Exception 2 of the New York City Building Code shall be permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for Assembly occupancies.

To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 403.1. Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. Fixture calculations in Group B office occupancies shall utilize the total occupant load on a given floor to determine the number of fixtures required for that floor.
Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

testCase.question: If the multipurpose room is permitted to be classified as Group B because it has fewer than 75 occupants, can its required plumbing fixtures be calculated using the normal Group B fixture requirements?
